newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to evacuate Americans from Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to evacuate Americans from Sierra Leone.

text.p: U.S. Marines using helicopters plan to evacuate about 250 American citizens from Freetown, Sierra Leone, to a warship offshore on Friday, the Pentagon said on Thursday.

"The situation (in Freetown) is not stable at all. There is a good deal of sporadic gunfire," said Army Col. Richard Bridges, a Pentagon spokesman. He said the U.S. helicopter carrier Kearsarge had arrived off the West African nation early on Thursday and added "we anticipate beginning the (evacuation) operation tomorrow and completing it tomorrow."

Bridges told reporters there were approximately 400 Americans in Sierra Leone, where democratic leaders were ousted in a military coup last weekend, and that about 250 had indicated they wanted to leave the country.
He said the Kearsarge, with more than 1,200 Marines on board, was about 20 miles (32 kms) offshore and that a four-man advance team from the ship had gone ashore to prepare for the evacuation.
The spokesman said there was no indication that Americans were being targeted, but "the randomness of the gunfire could put American citizens at risk."

He said the Americans would be taken to the Kearsarge and then moved within a day or two to Conakry in Guinea, about 100 miles 160 kms from Freetown, where they were expected to be flown back to the United States.
